questions.key_step: Ellipse-inside-rectangle containment
questions.justification: Read the bounding box of the ellipse and compare with the rectangle; one familiar picture, but three options to dispose of. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: Recognise $a+1=2(b+1)$ so chain length is bounded by powers of 2.
questions.justification: The recurrence has to be unrolled and linked to the divisibility bound $2^{k+1}\le101$; students often stop at 6 (as the PDF does). Nearest idea: shifted geometric recurrences (L3). (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: List $R$ row by row, then check diagonal pairs.
questions.justification: Bookkeeping over a $7\times7$ grid with an inequality; no insight needed but error-prone. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: List $R$ for $y=\max\{x,1\}$ and count missing pairs.
questions.justification: Short listing with an immediate pattern. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: Solve $y=2x$ or $2x-1$ within $A$, then count diagonal and reverse pairs.
questions.justification: Slightly longer listing than Q4 but the same method. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: Count pairs with max in $\{3,4\}$; disprove reflexive and transitive.
questions.justification: Counting plus two property checks for a two-statement option set. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: Count coprime pairs $(m,n)$, $m<n\le10$ (Farey-type count).
questions.justification: Careful systematic gcd count; the totient route shortens it. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: On an axis both conditions force $|t|=3$.
questions.justification: Immediate reading of the two regions; four points to sum. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: Count equivalence relations on 3 elements (partitions).
questions.justification: Standard counting of partitions of a 3-set; students must know the equivalence-partition link. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: Smallest equivalence relation containing $R$ forces $\{1,2,3\}$ into one class.
questions.justification: Closure under reflexive, symmetric and transitive requirements; short but needs care. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: Relation $b_1=b_2$ is 'same value of a function', so equivalence.
questions.justification: Immediate check of the three properties and the class is a horizontal line. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: $x+y$ even means same parity.
questions.justification: Standard textbook equivalence relation. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: Use $\sec^2-\tan^2=1$ to reduce to $\tan^2x=\tan^2y$.
questions.justification: Needs the trigonometric identity and chain of three properties. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: Range is a geometric progression with ratio $2/5$.
questions.justification: Convert the log relation to $y=(2/5)^x$ and sum a GP. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: Find counter-examples to symmetry and transitivity for an 'or' relation.
questions.justification: Three properties tested on $\mathbb N\times\mathbb N$ with an 'or' condition; counter-examples need a short search. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: Solve each linear relation inside $X$ and double the count.
questions.justification: List-and-count with simple Diophantine equations. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: Inclusion-exclusion with APs of multiples.
questions.justification: Routine inclusion-exclusion with arithmetic progressions. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: List $R$ for $4x\le5y$ and count missing reverses.
questions.justification: Short list on a $5\times5$ grid. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: Parity reduction of $3ad-7bc$, then find a valid transitivity counter-example in $A\times B$.
questions.justification: Algebraic parity argument for symmetry and a search for a counter-example in the product set. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)

questions.key_step: Empty set breaks reflexivity; overlap is not transitive.
questions.justification: Familiar 'overlap' relation on a power set; needs the empty-set case and a counter-example. (Level set on the user's 0-5 scale; concepts self-assigned.)
